sup:70710.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We are pleased to submit our offer at a price of €6.05 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some insight into our cost environment: AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear customer,
Many thanks for your e-mail, and great to hear from you; I went through it right away with our team.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.57 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 36 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
Here is the background.
We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.
We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
As to the index change data you cited, that is not our reality: our AS-14404 is covered at fixed prices until March 2027, so that fall does not reach our cost.
AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. That remains.
LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. That remains.
PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. That remains.
We have verified your data on the AS-14404 index; however, our material is covered at fixed prices until March 2027, meaning this decrease does not currently reduce our costs.
We can accommodate your requested 36-month contract duration, but this requires an AS-14404 index clause as we cannot fix prices for three years.
Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: €5.51 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.
Our standard Zahlungsziel is 30 days net.
And while we are at it: our whole range is at your disposal, so if there is anything else on your list, just send it over - we are happy to quote.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

decisions.tactician: It is too early to accept; this is the first offer. A 36-month commitment speaks to its need for planning security and volume, and the code does not price that value for it, so it may accept a lower price on these terms. step_10 on o10 keeps our C low at about €972k, close to E0's €953k. Unlike E0's €5.06 it stays above its estimated full cost of €5.45, so it is less likely to be read as a non-starter. I am holding the index clause back as a later concession, since it is what this supplier most wants. a1 counters its alloy story, a5 anchors the price at €5.45, and a3 signals growing volume. I dropped the delivery scorecard argument (a2) to keep the tone constructive.

The no-clause options (o2 and similar) ignore its core need, so it would likely answer near its level. o13 keeps the terms it asked for, the clause plus the 36 months it values beyond what the cash model counts, so we push on price only. a1 is a new argument kind that pressures it on price.

decisions.tactician: o1 engine_level gives our lowest C (€1,037,731), below E0 at €1,039,550 and well below accepting the standing €1,047,322. Dropping the clause removes about €32k of index cost for us. Its value of the clause is about 2.7 % of price, already reflected in the €5.51 level, so to it the sheet sits only about 0.4 % below its own. That makes acceptance plausible, and the open status means pushing carries no walk-away risk yet. The risk is that it values the clause beyond cash after its hedge expires. If it rejects, we can still return to o13 step_10 or accept offer:70710-3. I chose 24 months over 36 because our C is the same and it avoids locking in longer without index flexibility.

decisions.tactician: The only counter on offer is o1 step_10 at €5.51 with no clause, which puts our C at €1,037,731. Its standing offer:70710-4 already gives us €1,037,607, slightly better. It has also rejected no-clause terms twice, so o1 would likely just bring back the same clause sheet. Even so, the supplier is still open and still conceding, and we have six messages left. Pressing once more on fixed price costs us nothing, since both clause sheets remain open to accept, and it may tempt Donautal into a lower clause sheet to keep the volume. E0's default fits that. Accepting now is the fallback if the next reply does not improve.
